item.title: Binance Says Hackers Plotted $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist for Months
item.description: A report from the cryptocurrency exchange described a monthslong campaign involving fake job interviews that exploited an engineer’s work computer and an internal A.I. tool.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Gabby Jones/Bloomberg
item.media:description: The hackers used a computer and an internal A.I. tool to take control of the machines of two engineers on Binance’s wallet team.

item.title: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject A.I.
item.description: Google is making it easier to restrict its A.I. tools for students. But schools that block A.I. entirely will lose student access to Google’s search engine.
item.dc:creator: Dana Goldstein and Natasha Singer
item.media:credit: Carlos Barria/Reuters
item.media:description: Google products are ubiquitous in American schools.

item.title: Apple’s Profit Grows 12% Despite Component Price Worries
item.description: The company said iPhone sales remained strong, but warned that the cost of memory chips for its devices was going up.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: David Fouts for The New York Times
item.media:description: Apple’s new touch-screen MacBook Pro at a product launch in Los Angeles last week.

item.title: Inside Anthropic’s Hunt for A.I. Computing Power
item.description: The company went on a deal spree with tech giants, former crypto miners and others to gain computing power to further its artificial intelligence ambitions.
item.dc:creator: Sri Muppidi and Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: Illustration by Mark Harris; Photographs by Thea Traff for The New York Times, AJ Mast for The New York Times, Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times, Getty Images

item.title: Voting Problems Cause a Surge in Misleading Fraud Claims Online
item.description: Mentions of “cheat,” “steal,” “rig” and similar terms spiked on X this morning as voting began.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Set Up ‘War Rooms’ to Fight Disinfo About Midterm Elections
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed to protect Tuesday’s elections from efforts to undermine democracy.
item.dc:creator: Steven Lee Myers
item.media:credit: Heather Diehl for The New York Times
item.media:description: OpenAI employees work inside the company’s Election Operations Center in San Francisco.

item.title: Are Freezers Being Hacked? Europe and the U.S. Military Investigate.
item.description: A wave of disruptions at grocery stores, which some officials blame on cyberattacks, highlights the vulnerability of supply chains. Shops across Europe were affected again on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Ali Watkins
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Fred Tanneau/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Shelves were empty at a grocery store in Névez, France, last month after hundreds of supermarket refrigeration systems in the country were targeted.

item.title: Driven by A.I. Boom, Marvell and Lumentum Announce $115 Billion Merger
item.description: Marvell and Lumentum said they were combining, in a major bet on a technology, known as optical networking, that is increasingly being used in A.I. data centers.
item.dc:creator: Don Clark
item.category: Laser (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation)
item.media:credit: Eduardo Munoz/Reuters
item.media:description: Matt Murphy, chairman and chief executive of Marvell Technology, at the company’s investor day in New York last month.

item.title: Deportees Turn to TikTok to Document Life Starting Over
item.description: On TikTok, men and women sent back after living in the United States are documenting the reality of starting over — and finding an audience.
item.dc:creator: Isabella Kwai
item.media:credit: Heather Michelle Photography
item.media:description: Catherine Coe with her family in Tuscaloosa, Ala., before Mr. Benitez was deported in September of 2025.

item.title: Cyril Hilsum, Who Helped Invent Flat-Panel Displays in TVs and iPhones, Has Died at 101
item.description: The man who helped develop the technology for liquid crystal displays — the screens in flat-panel televisions and laptops — has died at 101.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Rosenwald
item.media:credit: via Hilsum Family
item.media:description: Cyril Hilsum with a fellow scientist in England in 1966. Known as “the father of liquid crystals,” he helped develop the technology that allowed electronic screens to go from bulky to svelte.

item.title: How Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Went Down
item.description: A war room. A global conference call. A founder who live-posted about the largest crypto heist in history. Inside a frantic 24 hours at the world’s biggest crypto exchange.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany
item.media:credit: SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg
item.media:description: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said $6.3 billion of funds are involved in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest-ever hack.

item.title: In San Francisco’s A.I. Boom, a First Date Has Become an Interview
item.description: When there is A.I. to build, who has time for romance? Techies are going out less and expecting more on each date — including a family health history.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: Fresh off a long relationship and wanting to keep things low-key, Amanda Chung, 25, said most of the men she had met in San Francisco wanted something serious “even if they aren’t ready for it yet.”

item.title: AO3 Fan Fiction Site Is Hacked and Could Be Offline for Weeks
item.description: Home to tales inspired by the likes of “Harry Potter” and “Heated Rivalry,” the archive was taken down after “an intrusion,” one of its founders said. It could be down for weeks.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Chao

item.title: House Democrats Criticize Justice Dept. Support of OpenAI in Copyright Suit
item.description: In a court filing, top Democrats on the Judiciary Committee indicated their support for publishers in a lawsuit led by The New York Times.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Lucas Foglia for The New York Times
item.media:description: The San Francisco offices of OpenAI, which is being sued in federal court by The New York Times and other publishers.

item.title: ‘You Can See Everything’: What Was Billy Evans Watching at 2x?
item.description: What was Elizabeth Holmes’s partner watching in the new Nathan Fielder documentary? We found the videos (and the scientists in them).
item.dc:creator: C.J. Robinson

item.title: Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Is Just the Start of a Risky New Era
item.description: The largest cyber heist in history came as attackers increasingly use artificial intelligence and other advanced techniques to steal crypto and quickly launder the funds.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany and Dustin Volz
item.media:credit: Tyrone Siu/Reuters
item.media:description: The founder of Binance, Changpeng Zhao, in Hong Kong in August. The company, the world’s biggest crypto exchange, has promised to make customers whole.

item.title: Polymarket and Kalshi Face a Major Accuracy Test: The Midterms
item.description: Studies have shown that the betting sites can predict races correctly, but their ability to forecast U.S. midterm elections is an important proving ground.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson
item.media:credit: Hilary Swift for The New York Times
item.media:description: Prediction platforms like Polymarket are hoping the U.S. midterm elections will be their moment to shine.

item.title: Are We in an A.I. Bubble? We’re About to Find Out.
item.description: “This is the first pure-play L.L.M. company to go public, to open its books so we can actually look at the underlying business of this A.I. boom.”
item.dc:creator: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Daniel Ramirez, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano and Alyssa Moxley
item.media:credit: Photo Illustration by The New York Times; Images: Anthropic, Getty Images

item.title: This Device Uses A.I. and Lasers to Kill Mosquitoes
item.description: A Chinese start-up has developed a device that uses artificial intelligence and lasers to kill mosquitoes. But there are safety concerns for people and other creatures nearby when the device is in action.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher, Nailah Morgan, Qilai Shen and Siyi Zhao
item.category: Laser (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation)

item.title: Binance Suspends Withdrawals After Crypto Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion
item.description: The crypto exchange said it was compromised in what could be the biggest crypto heist ever. One research lab attributed the theft to “North Korea’s elite hacking unit.”
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany and Ryan Mac
item.media:credit: Antonio Masiello/Getty Images
item.media:description: Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder, said the incident “does look like a hack.”

item.title: Intel’s Shares Plunge 20% as A.I. Hinders Some Parts of Its Business
item.description: The chipmaker, whose largest investor is the U.S. government, reported that the A.I. boom’s domino effect had hurt sales to personal computer makers.
item.dc:creator: Don Clark
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: A silicon wafer at Intel’s campus in Ocotillo, Ariz. The company reported revenue of $16.5 billion in its third quarter.

item.title: Big Tech’s Data Center Blitz Is Burning Through Cash and Scaring Wall St.
item.description: Amazon became the latest tech company to announce swelling investments in A.I. amid stumbling share prices.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Nathan Howard for The New York Times
item.media:description: Amazon is spending heavily on new data centers to operate with this one in Ashburn, Va.

item.title: Polymarket and Kalshi Turn Midterm Elections Into a Multimillion Dollar Market
item.description: Betting markets like Polymarket and Kalshi have transformed America’s democracy into a new kind of casino.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson and Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Hilary Swift for The New York Times
item.media:description: David Bensoussan has placed wagers worth over $1.5 million in over a dozen midterm races.

item.title: DoorDash to Buy Instacart for $17 Billion, Uniting 2 Delivery Giants
item.description: The deal combines the country’s largest restaurant delivery service with its biggest online grocery platform.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin and Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Amir Hamja/The New York Times
item.media:description: In its most recent quarter, DoorDash said it completed 970 million orders.

item.title: Hit the Road This Season With These Useful New Map Features
item.description: The recent updates to Google Maps and Apple’s Maps use artificial (and human) intelligence for better navigation, planning and travel guides.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:credit: Apple
item.media:description: The Flyover view in the latest version of Apple’s Maps app includes sharper aerial views of major cities so you can explore before you go.

item.title: Bodacious A.I. Bots Are Stealing Jokes From Young Female Comedians
item.description: Swiping jokes word for word, these bodacious bots mainly lift from young female comedians. What’s so insidious is how they’re subtly changing us, the audience.
item.dc:creator: Jason Zinoman

item.title: Alphabet’s Revenue Rises 25% as Profit Falls
item.description: The company has been spending relentlessly to build A.I. and said it would increase those investments next year. Profit dropped because of changes to the value of its investments.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Michael Hanson for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Google data center next to the Columbia River in The Dalles, Ore. “We’re excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us,” said Alphabet’s chief executive, Sundar Pichai.

item.title: Microsoft’s Profit Jumps 32% Despite Big Increase in Spending
item.description: The company’s free cash flow stayed positive in the last quarter even as it spent $45.2 billion on capital expenses like data centers and offered to pay workers to leave.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Grant Hindsley for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Redmond, Wash., campus of Microsoft, which reported $36.6 billion in profit for its latest quarter.

item.title: Apple Unveils Its First Touch-Screen MacBook Pro
item.description: Steve Jobs and Tim Cook both dismissed the idea, but Apple’s new chief executive is reimagining some of the company’s most important products.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang and Brian X. Chen
item.media:credit: David Fouts for The New York Times
item.media:description: The new Mac, with a starting price of $2,899, is the latest step into a new era for the consumer electronics giant.
